blocks.prompt: 7 A triangle has vertices at \(A(4, 1)\), \(B(-2, 5)\) and \(C(0, -3)\). Find the vertices of the reflected triangle over the \(y\)-axis using a transformation matrix.
blocks.explanation:
Yeh reflection ka sawal hai: \(y\)-axis ka transformation (reflection) matrix lagana hai.
Teen naye points (images) nikalne hain.
Plan: har vertex ko column likhein, \(\begin{bmatrix}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{bmatrix}\) se zarb dein, naye coordinates parhein, phir tasdeeq karein.
Sochiye: aaina (mirror) mein aap ka daayan haath baayan nazar aata hai, lekin aap ki oonchai wahi rehti hai. \(y\)-axis mein reflection bhi aisa hi hai: left-right (\(x\)) ulta hota hai, oopar-neeche (\(y\)) wahi rehta hai. Isi liye matrix ke pehle entry mein \(-1\) hai aur doosre mein \(+1\).
Dhyan dein: \(x\)-axis aur \(y\)-axis ke matrices aapas mein confuse na karein. \(x\)-axis mein reflection \(y\) ka sign badalta hai (matrix \(\begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{bmatrix}\)), aur \(y\)-axis mein reflection \(x\) ka sign. Point ko hamesha column matrix likh kar matrix ke right par rakhein, kyunke \(2 \times 2\) matrix sirf \(2 \times 1\) column se is tarteeb mein zarb hota hai. Jawab ko graph par bana kar dekhein to triangle \(y\)-axis ke doosri taraf bilkul usi shakal mein nazar aayega.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: triangle jis ke vertices \(A(4, 1)\), \(B(-2, 5)\), \(C(0, -3)\) hain.
Humein find karna hai: \(y\)-axis mein reflection (aks) ke baad naye vertices \(A'\), \(B'\), \(C'\).
Tareeqa: Har point ko column matrix bana kar \(y\)-axis wale reflection matrix se left side se zarb denge, bilkul Example 16 ki tarah.

\(y\)-axis ka reflection matrix
\[\begin{bmatrix}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{bmatrix}\]
Kyun: Yeh matrix \((x, y)\) ko \((-x, y)\) bana deta hai. \(y\)-axis aaina (mirror) hai: point aaine se jitna door tha utna hi door rehta hai, bas doosri taraf chala jata hai. Is liye sirf \(x\) ka sign badalta hai, \(y\) wahi rehta hai.

\(A\) ka image
\[A' = \begin{bmatrix}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}4 \\ 1\end{bmatrix}\]
\[= \begin{bmatrix}(-1)(4) + 0(1) \\ 0(4) + 1(1)\end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix}-4 \\ 1\end{bmatrix}\]
\[A' = (-4, 1)\]
Kyun: Matrix ki pehli row ko column se zarb karne par naya \(x\) milta hai, doosri row se naya \(y\). Dekhein ke sirf \(x\) ka sign badla hai.

\(B\) ka image
\[B' = \begin{bmatrix}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}-2 \\ 5\end{bmatrix}\]
\[= \begin{bmatrix}(-1)(-2) + 0(5) \\ 0(-2) + 1(5)\end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix}2 \\ 5\end{bmatrix}\]
\[B' = (2, 5)\]
Kyun: Matrix ki pehli row ko column se zarb karne par naya \(x\) milta hai, doosri row se naya \(y\). Dekhein ke sirf \(x\) ka sign badla hai.

\(C\) ka image
\[C' = \begin{bmatrix}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ -3\end{bmatrix}\]
\[= \begin{bmatrix}(-1)(0) + 0(-3) \\ 0(0) + 1(-3)\end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix}0 \\ -3\end{bmatrix}\]
\[C' = (0, -3)\]
Kyun: Matrix ki pehli row ko column se zarb karne par naya \(x\) milta hai, doosri row se naya \(y\). Dekhein ke sirf \(x\) ka sign badla hai.

Tasdeeq
\(A(4, 1) \to (-4, 1)\), \(B(-2, 5) \to (2, 5)\), \(C(0, -3) \to (0, -3)\).
Kyun: Har jore mein sirf \(x\) ka sign badla. \(C\) ka \(x = 0\) hai, yani woh khud \(y\)-axis (aaine) par hai, is liye apni jagah par hi rehta hai. Aaine par rakhi cheez ka aks usi jagah hota hai.
